Exploratory Analysis

Distribution of broadband rates, income-broadband scatter (r = 0.713), and education-broadband scatter. The strong correlation confirms income is the dominant individual-level predictor, but substantial variance remains.

Broadband Rate Distribution by County Type

KDE plots reveal structural heterogeneity: rural tracts concentrate below 0.40, suburban tracts span the threshold, and urban tracts are mostly well-served with a thin tail of affordability-suppressed outliers.

Moran Scatter Plot, Global Moran's I = 0.914

The steep positive slope (= Moran's I) confirms extreme spatial clustering. Points are coloured by LISA quadrant. LL cold spots (blue) cluster in the lower-left, low broadband with low-broadband neighbours.

LISA Cold Spot / Hot Spot Map

All 115 LL cold-spot tracts are rural (blue). All 95 HH hot-spot tracts are urban or suburban (red). Zero suburban or urban tracts form LL clusters, a critical finding for the guardrail analysis.

Secondary Outcome: Economic Disadvantage Index by LISA Cluster

LL cold-spot tracts have median EDI = 0.838, the highest multi-dimensional deprivation of any cluster type. Infrastructure grants to LL tracts address income, education, and broadband deficits simultaneously.

Subgroup OLS: R² and Income Coefficient by County Type

Rural OLS R² = 0.429 (highest); income coefficient in urban is 3.5× larger than rural (0.206 vs 0.059). Urban broadband is income-constrained, affordability is the binding driver, not infrastructure.

Spatial Regression Model Comparison

Spatial Lag outperforms OLS by 330 AIC points (−922 vs −592). ρ = 0.678 confirms direct spatial spillovers: a one-unit rise in neighbours' broadband raises own-tract adoption by 0.678 units.

Guardrail: LL-Cluster Targeting Misses 76.4% of Underserved Households

CRITICAL: LL targeting covers only 23.6% of underserved households. Suburban (234,282 HH) and urban (68,250 HH) underserved populations receive zero coverage because their tracts do not form spatial clusters.

Decision & Recommendation

Guardrail breach confirmed: LL-cluster targeting covers only 23% of underserved households. A pure spatial rule misses 77% of underserved people (401,987 households).
Spatial Lag confirms market failure: ρ = 0.677804, AIC improvement of 330 points over OLS. Place-based infrastructure intervention is warranted in rural LL clusters.
Hybrid policy required: Route BEAD infrastructure grants to all 115 LL rural cold-spot tracts. Route parallel affordability vouchers to suburban and urban tracts below the 65% broadband threshold.
